title: Noise operator as a kernel sum
statement:
Fix $\rho \in \bbr$, an arity $n$, and a point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$. For every Boolean
function $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the value of the noise operator $T_\rho$ at $x$
equals the kernel-weighted sum of $g$, namely
\[
  (T_\rho g)(x) \;=\; \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^n} K_\rho(x,y)\, g(y),
\]
where $K_\rho(x,y) = \prod_{i} \tfrac{1 + \rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$ is the
noise kernel and $\sigma$ is the $\pm 1$ sign encoding of a bit. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
replaced:
For every $g : \mathrm{BoolCube}\,n \to \bbr$ and every $x$,
\[
  (T_\rho g)(x) \;=\; \sum_{y} K_\rho(x,y)\, g(y).
\]
